item.title: R1-07-G3: Atlanta Braves 8, San Diego Padres 6
item.description: Played by Joe and sent to the co-managed tournament games chat as the app scorecard PDF plus the full graded play-by-play text on 2026-10-29; official R1-07 Game 3 under Joe's standing rule that sending a fixture's box score makes the game count. Box score record: the two sources carry the linescore, the full batting and pitching lines, and a complete play log, and they agree on every number. The decisions are not printed; they are derived from the play log (Warren Spahn pitched 8 innings and left with an 8-6 lead that Atlanta never lost, taking the win; Ed Whitson was charged with 6 runs in 2 innings and took the loss; Craig Kimbrel pitched a scoreless 9th with a 2-run lead for the save). Hank Aaron's solo homer in the 1st put Atlanta up 1-0; San Diego answered with 3 in the bottom half on four straight singles and Manny Machado's run-scoring forceout. Atlanta's 5-run 2nd all came off Whitson: Joe Torre reached on Adrian Gonzalez's 2-base error leading off, Dale Murphy hit a 2-run homer, and Chipper Jones hit a 3-run homer. Ozzie Albies homered off Luke Gregerson in the 4th, Machado's sacrifice fly in the 5th made it 7-4, Murphy homered again off Mike Adams in the 6th for 8-4, and San Diego closed to 8-6 in the 8th on Mark Loretta's RBI single and Fernando Tatis Jr.'s run-scoring forceout off Spahn before Kimbrel closed it. Earned runs: the scorecard charges Whitson only 2 earned runs of his 6; the Gonzalez error opened the Top 2 before the 5-run inning, and the card's earned-run treatment makes most of that inning unearned. The card governs every line, and the 2 earned runs are booked exactly as printed, not recomputed from the play log. Atlanta hit five homers (Aaron, Murphy twice, Chipper Jones's 3-run shot, Albies); San Diego hit none, and Machado's double was its only extra-base hit. Rabbit Maranville's stolen base is printed on the scorecard; the play log does not narrate the steal, so it rests on the card alone. Ozzie Albies's Top 9 double play is printed on the scorecard (GIDP: Ozzie Albies) and matches the play log. Steve Finley's Bot 4 bunt is scored a fielder's choice in the scorecard grid (the lead runner was forced), not a sacrifice, so no batter in this game has a sacrifice hit; Machado's sacrifice fly is printed in the scorecard extras and its grid (SF9) and is carried in the SF column. No hit batters: the scorecard grid prints HBP 0 for all nine pitchers, so HB 0 for all 9 pitchers and HBP 0 for all 18 batters are card-sourced values carried in the tables below, and the homer, hit batter, and derived plate appearance checks run on real data. One error in the game: Adrian Gonzalez (San Diego, 1B, Top 2, Torre reached on a 2-base error). Eric Show, San Diego's fifth starter in posted rotation order, threw 2 relief innings (the 8th and 9th); the play log names no new San Diego pitcher in the 9th. No substitutions on either side; all 18 starters finished. Game 2 availability was honored: Kid Nichols (27 outs in Game 2) and Randy Jones (9 outs in Game 2), both unavailable under the house outs convention, did not pitch. Managers: Bobby Cox (Atlanta) and Bruce Bochy (San Diego). Venue is Petco Park. Atlanta leads the series 3-0.

item.title: R1-07-G2: San Diego Padres 3, Atlanta Braves 8

The only sacrifice was Tony Gwynn's Top 6 bunt, printed in the box as SH and carried in the SH column; no sacrifice flies anywhere in the play log, so SF is 0 for every batter. No errors by either club. No substitutions on either side; all 18 starters finished. Game 1 availability was honored: Greg Maddux and Jake Peavy, both unavailable off their Game 1 outs, did not pitch. Managers: Bobby Cox (Atlanta) and Bruce Bochy (San Diego). Venue is Truist Park. item.title: R1-06-G5: Montreal Expos 2, Chicago Cubs 3
item.description: Played by Joe and sent to the co-managed tournament games chat as the app scorecard PDF plus the full graded play-by-play text on 2026-10-29; official R1-06 Game 5 under Joe's standing rule that sending a fixture's box score makes the game count, and the game closes the series. Box score record: the two sources carry the linescore, the full batting and pitching lines, and a complete play log, and they agree on every number. The decisions are not printed; they are derived from the play log (Mordecai Brown entered the top of the 9th with two outs and the game tied 2-2, retired Jose Vidro for the final out, and was the pitcher of record when Chicago walked it off; Jeff Reardon pitched the 8th and 9th for Montreal and the winning run is his; no save). Chicago scored in the 2nd (Hack Wilson single scoring Sammy Sosa), the 7th (Wilson single scoring Billy Williams), and the 9th: Wilson singled, Gabby Hartnett popped out, and Andre Dawson doubled on the hit and run to score Wilson with the walk-off run. Montreal scored twice in the 6th: Larry Walker tripled off Carlos Zambrano and scored on Andre Dawson's single off Pedro Strop, and Dawson scored on Gary Carter's single. Andre Dawson appears in BOTH lineups again, as in Game 4: he batted 9th for Chicago (1-for-4, the walk-off double, 1 RBI) and 5th for Montreal (1-for-4, 1 RBI, 1 stolen base). Joe ruled in chat on 2026-10-29 (the Game 4 ruling): they are different teams, and the game counts exactly as played, Dawson on both sides. The two printed tables fold hit batters into the BB column, the same fold as Game 4: the batting table prints Billy Williams BB 2 and the pitching table prints Jeff Reardon BB 1, and the play log proves one of those walks is the same hit batter, Williams hit by a Reardon pitch in the Bot 8; Williams walked once for real (Bot 7) and Reardon issued no real walk. So Williams is BB 1, HBP 1 and Reardon is BB 0, HB 1, carried split in the tables below with the play log as the source. Every other walk in the game is a real walk (Chicago batting: Sosa 2; Montreal batting: Guerrero 2, Raines 1; pitching: Vazquez 3, Zambrano 2, Lee Smith 1), and with the split walks tie 3 and 3 and hit batters tie 1 and 1. Sacrifices are printed in the source: SH Gary Carter (Top 4) and SH Gabby Hartnett (Bot 7); no sacrifice flies. Errors: one per club, as printed on the scorecard: Gary Carter (Montreal) and Ron Santo (Chicago, Top 3, Tim Raines reached). No substitutions on either side; all 18 starters finished. Mark Grace started at first base for Chicago; Anthony Rizzo and Pete Crow-Armstrong did not appear. Game 4 availability was honored: Pete Alexander, Bryn Smith, and Andy McGaffigan did not pitch. Bruce Sutter was charged with one wild pitch (printed on the scorecard). Venue is Wrigley Field. Chicago wins the series 4-1; series run totals are Chicago 24, Montreal 15 (Chicago 5, 2, 5, 9, 3; Montreal 4, 4, 4, 1, 2).
